title: GLINT-RU: Gated Lightweight Intelligent Recurrent Units for Sequential Recommender Systems

problem.claim: Sequential recommender systems need to capture user-item interactions while controlling computational cost and inference latency.

gap.claim: Existing efficient approaches struggle to embed high-quality semantic and positional information into latent representations.

contributions.claim: GLINT-RU is a lightweight sequential recommender system using a single-layer dense selective GRU module to accelerate inference.
A dense selective gate adaptively captures temporal dependencies and fine-grained positional information for latent representations.
A parallel mixing block infuses fine-grained positional features into user-item interactions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on three datasets reportedly show superior prediction accuracy and inference speed compared with RNN, Transformer, MLP, and SSM baselines.
The authors characterize GLINT-RU as a powerful and efficient solution for sequential recommender systems.
Implementation code is reported as publicly available for reproducibility.

narrative_sequence.summary: Transformer-based models are effective for sequential recommendation but have high computational costs and slow inference.
Efficient sequential recommender approaches struggle with semantic and positional representation quality.
GLINT-RU addresses these challenges with a dense selective GRU, adaptive gating, and a parallel positional-feature mixing block.
The authors report improved accuracy and inference speed across three datasets against several model families.
The implementation is reported as publicly available.
